requirements.title: Procedure binding labels name BIND procedures to the companion processor
requirements.source: S18.10.2 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF546.
requirements.definition: The binding label of a procedure is a default character value specifying the name by which a procedure with the BIND attribute is known to the companion processor.

pending.procedure-binding-label-companion-name: Mixed C plan calls Fortran procedure with external label fort_proc_label; Fortran defines subroutine local_name() bind(C, name="fort_proc_label") that sets a BIND(C) integer flag to 269, and C observes the flag.

requirements.title: NAME= gives a nonblank trimmed binding label for procedures
requirements.source: S18.10.2 p2.name-specifier-trimmed-nonzero-label; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF546.
requirements.definition: For a procedure with BIND and a NAME= expression whose value has nonzero length after discarding leading and trailing blanks, that trimmed value is the binding label.

pending.procedure-name-specifier-trimmed-label: After guarding C_INT > 0 before any C_INT-kind declaration, Fortran defines integer(c_int) function local_cf_x() bind(C, name="  cf_x  ") returning 301; C declares int cf_x(void), calls cf_x(), and observes 301, proving the exact binding label is cf_x after discarding leading and trailing blanks.

requirements.title: BIND procedures without NAME= use lower-case procedure names as labels for eligible procedure kinds
requirements.definition: For a BIND procedure without NAME= that is not a dummy procedure, internal procedure, or procedure pointer, the binding label is the procedure name converted to lower case letters.

requirements.title: Procedures outside the BIND label cases have no binding label
requirements.source: S18.10.2 p2.no-label-otherwise; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF546.
requirements.definition: A procedure has no binding label outside the nonblank NAME= case and the eligible BIND-without-NAME= external procedure case.

pending.procedure-no-binding-label-otherwise: For BIND(C, NAME=""), the NAME= expression has zero length after blank trimming, so the procedure has no binding label and cannot be referenced from C by name. Fortran-side observation remains available: after guarding C_INT > 0 before any C_INT-kind declaration, a Fortran caller invokes integer(c_int) function local_empty() bind(C, name="") through its Fortran interface and observes result 307; no C source is linked that attempts a named reference to local_empty.

requirements.title: Submodule procedures with binding labels require an ancestor-module interface
requirements.source: S18.10.2 C1807; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF546.
requirements.definition: A procedure defined in a submodule shall not have a binding label unless its interface is declared in the ancestor module.

pending.submodule-binding-label-requires-ancesto: Rejected diagnostic plan: module m declares only an anchor module procedure, parent submodule declares interface module subroutine s() bind(C, name="s_label"), and child submodule defines module procedure s. Positive control changes only the constrained placement by moving that identical s interface into module m; all interface blocks remain in specification parts before CONTAINS, each procedure has a single interface declaration, and both procedure bodies use MODULE PROCEDURE without redeclaring type or arguments, so the control itself is conforming.

requirements.title: C function binding labels are the C function names
requirements.source: S18.10.2 p3; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF546.
requirements.definition: The binding label for a C function whose name has external linkage is the same as the C function name.
